headlines.text: Venus Williams bows out of US Open with straight-sets defeat to Sofia Kenin. The 46-year-old US veteran loses to wildcard compatriot but will play in women's doubles with sister Serena Williams.
Iran attacks Jordan, UAE after US bombs Larak Island: What’s the latest?. The retaliatory attacks came after the US targeted two Iranian launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz.
Kazakhstan’s Tokayev appoints longtime adviser as vice president. Erlan Karin has served as a top ⁠⁠aide to Tokayev since he took over the presidency in 2019.
Xi, Modi and Putin set to meet for SCO summit: What’s on the agenda?. The two-day summit aims to promote a vision of a multipolar world and mutual trade ties amid Trump's unilateralism.
England vs Pakistan second Test: Three talking points from cricket series. Pakistan’s batting collapses, concerns over the Lord’s pitch and Ollie Robinson’s rampant form highlight the series.
Syria is choosing diplomacy with Israel, but can its approach last?. Israel has attacked Syria, occupied its south since the al-Assad regime's ouster, testing Syria's diplomatic outreach.
Nord Stream bombings put Ukraine’s ties with Germany under pressure. The blasts strain ties with Ukraine and have exposed the risks of relying on Russian gas, analysts say.
‘An act of resistance’: Raja Shehadeh’s Palestinian diaries find a new home. Al Jazeera interviews the leading writer and lawyer, 75, in Edinburgh, where his daily documentation is being archived.
Nepal races to rescue trapped workers, as flood death toll surpasses 900. Nepal officials say rescuers focusing on reaching workers in hydropower project tunnels in flood-stricken region.
FIFA president Infantino ‘must go’, says former UEFA boss Platini. In a scathing interview, French great Michel Platini accuses Infantino of always loving 'money and power'.
Aston Villa vs Arsenal: Premier League – prediction, team news, lineups. Declan Rice continues to star for Arsenal, who may add Julian Alvarez to ranks, but hosts Villa are sore from sales.
Tennis great Djokovic exits US Open in first round amid tears and pain. Novak Djokovic's pursuit of a 25th Grand Slam ends in a five-set defeat to unseeded Argentinian player Mariano Navone.
Global coral reef coverage risks irreversible decline, new report warns. Coral reefs make up just 1 percent of ocean coverage, but host a quarter of all life in the sea.
People return to their flood-ravaged homes in Nepal. Survivors in Nepal’s Nuwakot district are digging through mud and debris for belongings left behind by flash floods.
Russia, China leaders to meet at Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit. The organisation is not officially anti-West, but Russian and Chinese leaders have used it to amplify their worldview.
A 12TB Steam “teraleak” spills more than a decade of lost PC gaming history. Cut content from Portal 2, hints of Half Life 2: Episode 3, and so much more.
Why it matters that President Trump just dialed into a NASA news conference. With just one more major mission upcoming, NASA's science programs need a boost.
Inside Meta’s push to put robots to work in data centers. The company is testing robots on tasks that can performed by technicians.
I asked 100 companies for my data. Some deleted it instead.. Testing 100 companies found privacy requests often led to confusion and dead ends.
Court rules Kalshi sports bets aren't "swaps," just gambling with a different name. Kalshi can't evade Nevada gambling laws by calling bets "swaps," judges rule.
Cities terminate Flock contracts at record pace in August. Cancellations have accelerated.
"RFK Jr. has lied to the Senate": Lawmakers call for criminal probe, ouster. RFK Jr. went to Samoa to spread vaccine fears. The measles outbreak after killed 83.
Trump blacklisting of "woke" Anthropic deemed illegal by federal judge. Anthropic refused to support lethal autonomous warfare and mass surveillance.
Here's what we know about the "space academy" Trump just announced. "It's called the US Space Academy. That's a big deal."
Apple One and Apple TV subscription prices increase by up to 20 percent. Annual Apple TV subscriptions get the biggest bump.
Our 10 favorite scenes from T2: Judgment Day. James Cameron's 1991 sci-fi blockbuster returns to theaters this weekend for its 35th anniversary.
Meta makes AI glasses slightly less creepy with limit on nonconsensual recording. Meta fixes AI glasses to stop recording any time users cover up the safety light.
Authorities arrest 2 alleged members of prolific hacking group TeamPCP. The group infected more than 1,000 organizations in a relentless supply-chain attack campaign.
Rocket Report: Europe splashes some cash on launch startups; Pallas-1 nears debut. "From here on, Starlink missions out of Florida will fly on Starship."
Anthropic's new hardware standard lets AI agents control the physical world. Standardized driver interface aims to let devices talk to AI and each other.
Google Maps Now Shows ‘Lake America’ Instead of Lake Ontario. After Donald Trump’s executive order demanding the name change, Google is the first major online map provider to flip the switch.

Best Mesh Wi-Fi Systems (2026): I Tested Them All. Forget about patchy internet connections and dead spots in the house. These WIRED-tested, multi-room mesh Wi-Fi systems will keep your whole house online.

The data center fight could decide the next president and cost America the AI race. Rising electric bills and data center construction spark bipartisan pushback from governors, but restricting AI infrastructure could cost America its lead.

GOV MIKE DUNLEAVY: China is holding critical minerals hostage. Alaska can help end the threat. Gov. Mike Dunleavy says Alaska hosts 57 of 60 critical minerals and argues developing them is essential to countering China's economic blackmail.

Inside the dangerous US mission that cleared Iran’s mines from Hormuz shipping lanes. CENTCOM's Adm. Brad Cooper details how Navy divers, SEALs and air power quietly cleared Iranian sea mines from the Strait of Hormuz shipping lanes.

My family fled the ‘butchers’ in Iran 50 years ago. We can’t give them what they want. On Tuesday, Aug. 25, Trump announced the U.S. Navy cleared every Iranian mine from the Strait of Hormuz, but the regime's attrition strategy looms.

Abdul El-Sayed shares dozens of donors with ex-GOP candidate at center of antisemitism controversy. Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and Dan Bilzerian share nearly two dozen donors who gave more than $61,000 combined to both campaigns.

Dozens of illegal alien truck drivers busted with licenses from deep blue states. Arizona's Yuma Sector bust netted 95 illegal alien truck drivers with state-issued CDLs, seizing methamphetamine and marijuana in smuggling crackdown.

Duffy teases 'unprecedented fraud crackdown' announcement with DHS, DOJ. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy teased a multi-agency fraud crackdown involving DHS, DOJ and ICE that is set to be announced on Monday.

Accused NC killer mom plans insanity defense — as retired judge says more may follow Lindsay Clancy strategy. Andrea Faust's insanity defense in her son's killing draws direct parallels to Lindsay Clancy's postpartum psychosis case as jurors deliberate.

Rockies player benched after flipping off Braves fans, caught on video giving the bird. Cole Carrigg flipped off Atlanta Braves fans after a costly eighth-inning misplay, and Rockies manager Warren Schaeffer pulled him from the lineup.

Many are making the argument that Jordan Travis was the greatest college QB of all time, and they aren't wrong. Jordan Travis posted a 29-10 record with Florida State's Mike Norvell, but FSU has gone 8-17 since his departure from the Seminoles program.

Parkgoer airlifted after Batman roller coaster incident leaves man with fractures to both legs. A 49-year-old visitor was airlifted to a hospital after suffering fractures in both legs on a Batman-themed roller coaster in Spain, lcoal reports say.

Beloved Texas chiropractor, hiking group among those unaccounted for after Grand Canyon flash flood. Dr. John Giusti's wife said the Texas chiropractor and his hiking group are among those missing after a flash flood tore through the Grand Canyon.

California mom has both legs amputated after suspected impaired driver plows into her restaurant lunch table. A California woman underwent three surgeries and a bilateral leg amputation after an alleged impaired driver crashed into a Boyle Heights restaurant.

Hasan Piker insists Abdul El-Sayed asked him to 'stump' for Michigan campaign amid backlash. Hasan Piker claimed Abdul El-Sayed asked him to stump for his Michigan U.S. Senate campaign before the Twitch streamer faced intense political backlash.

Nicolás Maduro flashes peace signs in first prison photos since US capture in Caracas. Ousted Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro appeared in his first photos from a New York prison, smiling as he awaits trial on federal drug trafficking charges.

Why too many women are prescribed antibiotics for UTIs they don't have. A recent study found that many women treated for recurrent UTIs didn't have UTIs at all. Instead, their symptoms were caused by hormonally driven inflammation and pelvic floor dysfunction.

Singapore is scrambling to stabilize birthrates. Experts say there are lessons for the U.S.. Singapore has unveiled a national initiative built entirely around its collapsing birthrate. Some demographers say the plan includes policy ideas that could help American parents.

Hit shows from Edinburgh's Fringe festival are coming to America. Here are our top picks. The annual "anything goes" performing arts festival featured more than 4,200 performances this year. These are the ones we're still talking about.

NPR spent 2 years tracking deaths from heat. We found a staggering hidden toll. An NPR investigation found that people in the U.S. are dying from heat much more often than official counts show. We explore the reasons why — and how lives can be saved.

The U.S. Venezuela oil deal won't lower your gas prices. Here's what you need to know. The Trump administration announced a deal Friday to develop a vast amount of Venezuela's oil reserves, with the U.S. taking a majority stake. Energy experts say there are many reasons to be skeptical.

Morning news brief. Trump says U.S. struck a deal to take control of 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil, U.S. and Iran resume exchanging strikes, funding at the top of the agenda as House reconvenes.

Arizona's taps won't run dry, but water bills will go up under federal plan for Colorado River. New federal rules mean Arizona will be getting a lot less water from the Colorado river. City leaders say they've been planning for years and no one will run out, but keeping taps flowing is expensive.

What Argentina gets right about youth soccer — and what the U.S. gets wrong. Argentina has produced some of the world's greatest soccer players. Could its youth system offer lessons for the United States?

Families of pilgrims likely caught in floods are desperate for news from Nepal. Four days after catastrophic floods wiped out villages along the Nepal-China border, thousands are still missing. Families look for answers but hear nothing.

Canada claps back at Trump's efforts to rename Lake Ontario as 'Lake America'. Ontario Premier Doug Ford has unveiled a giant billboard reading: "Lake Ontario — Now and Always." But tech giant Google has said it is renaming the lake for U.S. users, as President Trump demanded.
